description.narrative: The objective of the project is to support African countries to mobilize climate finance by providing evidence for climate finance mobilized in Africa in 2021 and 2022 and measuring progress from the last baseline estimates. This will also enable trend analysis which will provide insights on areas that are progressing versus those that are stalling. The aim is to identify gaps and opportunities and provide strategic policy recommendations for effective investments. The exercise, as a public good, will also aim to amplify knowledge globally and bridge the collective knowledge gap on climate financing flows and needs into Africa for better collaborative action.

activity-date.narrative: Assess the state of mitigation and adaptation finance in Africa leveraging CPI’s Global Landscape of Climate Finance Database (for 2021 and 2022), that contains the actual primary flows directed towards low-carbon and climate-resilient development interventions.

recipient-region.narrative: As before, the new Landscape will highlight the role of MDBs and DFIs as providers of climate finance in Africa (and the kinds of instruments they prefer to use) and will therefore help inform the ongoing discussions around MDB reform. Critically, the new Landscape will show whether there has been any improvement in private sector climate financing in Africa and whether private capital is starting to flow to (i) other climate-relevant sectors (such as nature) rather than being so heavily skewed to energy, and (ii) to other African countries besides those (such as South Africa, Nigeria, Kenya, Egypt etc.) that have been much more successful at raising climate finance. The rich analysis from this research will benefit anyone interested in climate finance in Africa in multiple ways, as has already been explained.
